about.description:
libze_intel_npu.so is the userspace Level Zero plugin that the
oneAPI Level Zero loader dlopens to talk to Intel NPU (VPU) hardware
on Meteor Lake, Arrow Lake, Lunar Lake, Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake
CPUs through the in-tree intel_vpu Linux kernel module
(/dev/accel/accel*).

This package only ships the userspace driver. To actually run
OpenVINO inference on NPU, two further pieces are required at runtime:
  * libnpu_driver_compiler.so — packaged separately as
    intel-driver-compiler-npu (forthcoming).
  * Firmware blobs at /lib/firmware/intel/vpu/*.bin — loaded by the
    kernel itself, so they cannot live inside a conda environment.
    Install them system-wide (linux-firmware, or the intel-fw-npu
    .deb from intel/linux-npu-driver releases on Ubuntu).
about.summary: Intel Level Zero userspace driver for NPU hardware

name: intel-level-zero-npu
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

# Single-output recipe: ships only the Level Zero userspace driver
# (libze_intel_npu.so) for Intel NPU. Two pieces of the upstream stack
# are intentionally omitted:
#
#   * libnpu_driver_compiler.so — the LLVM/MLIR-based NPU compiler. Heavy
#     to build (pulls in a full OpenVINO + npu_compiler tree). To be
#     added in a follow-up recipe (intel-driver-compiler-npu).
#   * intel-fw-npu firmware blobs — installed to /lib/firmware/intel/vpu/.
#     The kernel loads these at probe time and cannot read $CONDA_PREFIX,
#     so they cannot live in a conda environment. Users must install them
#     system-wide (linux-firmware or the intel-fw-npu .deb on Ubuntu).
#
# Test-only deps (validation/umd-test) are not built. Patch 0001 makes
# those guarded by ENABLE_VALIDATION_BUILD instead of unconditionally
# pulled, so we can drop the third_party/googletest and third_party/
# yaml-cpp submodules from the source tree.  yaml-cpp, if ever wanted,
# is available on conda-forge.

context:
  version: "1.38.0"
  # Submodule revisions as pinned by upstream at tag v${{ version }} (see
  # `git ls-tree v${{ version }} third_party/` in intel/linux-npu-driver).
  # These must be bumped alongside `version`.
  lze_npu_extensions_rev: "f9ad3bf89c2418d714aef2e6b96a5aafb12a1971"
  npu_compiler_elf_rev: "d325f45f2cb405b5fa2ff17a30de9469f1641b73"

package:
  name: intel-level-zero-npu
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  # rattler-build (like conda-build) hoists the single top-level directory
  # out of the archive, so the upstream tree lands directly in $SRC_DIR and
  # the vendored third_party sources below drop straight into it.
  #
  # Deliberately no `target_directory` here: any wrapper directory would
  # have to be spelled out again in the patch paths, the license_file paths
  # below and a `cd` in build.sh. Keeping the upstream root at $SRC_DIR
  # means the patches are plain upstream-relative diffs -- they can be
  # regenerated with `git format-patch` against an intel/linux-npu-driver
  # checkout and sent upstream as-is, and a version bump can never
  # invalidate their paths.
  - url: https://github.com/intel/linux-npu-driver/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 5584d03dcd37893b49cdb5f327578ab9afbc4a055d0fb66714e17c98c2821fd4
    patches:
      - patches/0001-third_party-only-pull-test-only-deps-when-tests-on.patch
      - patches/0002-umd-gate-unit_tests-on-ENABLE_NPU_UNIT_TESTS.patch
      # Upstream forces CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release and then appends -g in
      # umd/CMakeLists.txt, so every build is really RelWithDebInfo and the
      # LTO link is slower. With this applied libze_intel_npu.so.1.35.0 is
      # 1.6 MB with no .debug_* sections; without it, 21.3 MB.
      #
      # CAUTION: this patch must not be a pure-deletion diff. rattler-build
      # silently no-ops a patch whose hunks only remove lines -- it logs
      # "Applying patch: ..." and changes nothing, so the build succeeds
      # and quietly ships the 21.3 MB library. (git apply/git am handle it
      # fine, so it cannot be caught by testing the patch locally.) That is
      # why the two -g lines are replaced by a comment rather than simply
      # dropped. Keep at least one added line in every hunk here.
      - patches/0004-umd-do-not-add-g-to-Release-builds.patch
      # The driver targets Level Zero 1.27.0 but is built here against the
      # newer conda-forge level-zero (matching the runtime loader), whose
      # DDI tables have members the driver leaves null. Keep that warning
      # non-fatal instead of failing the -Werror build.
      - patches/0005-relax-missing-field-initializers-for-newer-level-zero.patch
      # 1.35.0 added a [tid:] field to the NPU_LOG output using glibc's
      # gettid() wrapper, which only exists from glibc 2.30. conda-forge
      # builds against the 2.17 sysroot, so use the raw syscall there.
      - patches/0006-log-use-syscall-gettid-on-glibc-older-than-2.30.patch
  # third_party/level-zero-npu-extensions: NPU-specific Level Zero
  # extension headers. Not packaged separately on conda-forge; carried
  # as a vendored source archive at the upstream-pinned rev.
  - url: https://github.com/intel/level-zero-vpu-extensions/archive/${{ lze_npu_extensions_rev }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 3255ea26d1d530a57a6558573cc233b717ecd34bf7adafd9401887ee4ddf5d6b
    target_directory: third_party/level-zero-npu-extensions
  # third_party/npu_compiler_elf: small Apache-2.0 ELF reader/writer +
  # VPUX loader, statically linked into libze_intel_npu.so. Upstream is
  # structured to be add_subdirectory()'d from this parent project (no
  # standalone install / CMake config), so vendor at build-time instead
  # of cutting a separate conda-forge package.
  - url: https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/npu_compiler_elf/archive/${{ npu_compiler_elf_rev }}.tar.gz
    sha256: c3da6c465b4533a0cc2ca98eaddf91caf0beeb4ac8a561caff21972781e23608
    target_directory: third_party/npu_compiler_elf

build:
  number: 0
  # Only the Linux userspace driver is supported (x86 intrinsics like
  # -msse4.2 / -mwaitpkg; conda-forge only builds linux-64 here). The bare
  # boolean form lets conda-smithy prune osx/win from the CI matrix.
  skip: not linux64
  # Intel follows the oneAPI Level Zero SOVERSION = MAJOR convention:
  # libze_intel_npu sets SOVERSION = PROJECT_VERSION_MAJOR in cmake, so
  # the .so SONAME is libze_intel_npu.so.1. ABI is guaranteed within a
  # major version; minor and patch bumps are backwards-compatible. So
  # pin downstream consumers to the same major only (see run_exports).

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - cmake
    - ninja
    - pkg-config
  host:
    - level-zero-devel
  run_exports:
    - ${{ pin_subpackage('intel-level-zero-npu', upper_bound='x') }}

tests:
  - requirements:
      run:
        # nm, to inspect the driver's dynamic symbols in the check below
        - binutils
    script:
      - test -f $PREFIX/lib/libze_intel_npu.so
      # Regression guard for the LTO / static-archive-index bug that
      # CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION fixes: libze_intel_npu.so
      # statically links the driver's own
      # implementation (the L0:: and VPU:: C++ classes, mangled _ZN2L0 /
      # _ZN3VPU) out of liblevel_zero_driver.a / libvpu_driver.a. If those
      # archives are indexed by a non-LTO-plugin-aware `ar`, the members
      # are never pulled and ~250 of these symbols come back UNDEFINED (U)
      # in the final library. A correctly linked driver has zero undefined
      # L0::/VPU:: symbols, so fail the build if any remain.
      - test -z "$(nm -D -u $PREFIX/lib/libze_intel_npu.so | grep -E '_ZN2L0|_ZN3VPU')"

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/intel/linux-npu-driver
  summary: Intel Level Zero userspace driver for NPU hardware
  description: |
    libze_intel_npu.so is the userspace Level Zero plugin that the
    oneAPI Level Zero loader dlopens to talk to Intel NPU (VPU) hardware
    on Meteor Lake, Arrow Lake, Lunar Lake, Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake
    CPUs through the in-tree intel_vpu Linux kernel module
    (/dev/accel/accel*).

    This package only ships the userspace driver. To actually run
    OpenVINO inference on NPU, two further pieces are required at runtime:
      * libnpu_driver_compiler.so — packaged separately as
        intel-driver-compiler-npu (forthcoming).
      * Firmware blobs at /lib/firmware/intel/vpu/*.bin — loaded by the
        kernel itself, so they cannot live inside a conda environment.
        Install them system-wide (linux-firmware, or the intel-fw-npu
        .deb from intel/linux-npu-driver releases on Ubuntu).
  license: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE.md
    # Vendored at build-time only (not packaged as separate conda
    # outputs); ship their LICENSE files alongside.
    - third_party/level-zero-npu-extensions/LICENSE.txt
    # Upstream spells this one "LICENCE".
    - third_party/npu_compiler_elf/LICENCE
  repository: https://github.com/intel/linux-npu-driver

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - hmaarrfk
